context: Hiroshi-elder takes Sho-young to see his old high school in Kansai.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、ここで卒業したの?
lines.en: Grandpa, did you graduate from here?
lines.style: Bright, earnest curiosity. Slightly awestruck at being in a grown-up place. Clear voice, open vowels, leans in with genuine interest.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: おう、若い頃の充実した日々や。
lines.en: Yeah — those were full days when I was young.
lines.style: Warm, unhurried Kansai drawl. Slight smile in the voice. Eyes distant with memory. Weight of fondness on each word, no rush to finish.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: What was the most important thing you learned?
lines.style: Soft, genuinely asking — not showing off. Leans into the question like he already suspects the answer matters. Steady breath, patient.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 友達、関心、ようけ持って、生きること。
lines.en: Friends, curiosity, holding on to plenty of both — that's how you live.
lines.style: Gentle Kansai lilt, deliberate pacing. Each phrase carries its own weight. Quiet conviction underneath. Sounds like wisdom arriving slowly, not being delivered.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Did you have a strict teacher?
lines.style: Soft, probing question. Not afraid of the answer. Small voice, big interest. Tilts head slightly in the tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: おう、頂いた言葉、今でも、生きる。
lines.en: Yeah — the words he gave me, I still carry them with me.
lines.style: Kansai warmth, reverent but not heavy. Slight catch on 'gave' — acknowledging the gift. Slow, measured delivery. Gratitude sitting underneath every syllable.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: いいなぁ、僕も、ええ友達持ちたい!
lines.en: That's so nice. I want to have good friends like that too!
lines.style: Sudden brightness, determination breaking through. Small voice with big feeling. Hopeful, earnest, a little awed at his own realization. Quick-paced final phrase.
